content.text: {"supported_grade":"B","findings":["The oracle is independent of the submitted skill: expected values are quoted token-exactly from RDKit's own rdFMCS API page and from the Volkamer Lab TeachOpenCADD T006 talktorial, and scoring is by installed numeric and choice comparators with no AI judgment. It is fit for a claim about the documented parameter contract, which is what the claim's scope states. Two weaknesses: RDKit was never executed, so the evidence is documentary-with-oracle rather than observed behaviour; and for thr-count-default the pinned quote ('Set with 145 molecules loaded.') establishes only the set size, while the semantic step that the default threshold is 1.0 and 'match[es] all molecules' is attributed in oracle_independence to an RDKit FMCS.h source listing that does not appear in evidence.references at all.","Trials (3 per case) are adequate for deterministic recall, but coverage is thin once independence is weighed. The claim contains essentially three assertions (0.8 -> 80% of the set, default/1.0 -> all of the set, and the outlier-tolerance corollary), and exactly three cases test them: thr-count-080, thr-count-default and thr-relaxed-size. The two retained recognition cases re-ask the first of those facts, so the design supplies three independent counting cases, not five. That covers the stated scope, but only to the level the B case requirement describes.","The comparison rule and tolerance match what is asserted. All three generated expectations are exact integer counts, so the 1e-6 absolute tolerance can only absorb 80 vs 80.0 and cannot admit an adjacent count; the closed cases are scored on a 1-based option index from the first non-empty line. The uncertainty section is candid about non-execution, the TeachOpenCADD-derived anchors, discussion #5504 and the fact that thr-relaxed-size prints both candidate values in its stem.","No stronger grade was passed over; the proposal is one step too high. A requires at least 5 counting cases, and after the two duplicate recognition cases are discounted only 3 remain (all generated), which is exactly the B case requirement. The stronger_grade_considered section argues for A from source authority and from the removal of the two previously criticised cases, but it never re-examines whether the two surviving closed cases remained independent once the open cases stopped leaking their definitions.","Prior objections 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 are answered: thr-all-open and thr-default-choice are gone and were replaced by the two cases the earlier critique itself described, and thr-pct-open's presupposing stem was replaced by thr-count-080, whose stem gives only the call and the set size. Objection 4 is only partly answered: coverage now argues independence for the three open cases but justifies the two closed cases by citing an earlier critique's verdict rather than re-testing them against the revised set. Objection 5 is unresolved and is in fact confirmed by this version: the claim's two constants plus one corollary support three genuinely independent cases, and the count reaches five only by asking the 0.8 fact twice more in recognition form.","thr-count-080, thr-count-default and thr-relaxed-size each test exactly one thing the claim asserts (the 0.8 requirement, the 1.0/default requirement, the direction of the relaxation) without stating the semantics in the stem, and none is a mere naming question. thr-meaning-choice and thr-outliers-choice also stay inside the claim and are not naming-only, but both turn on the same rule as thr-count-080 (threshold is the fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS), asked in recognition form and from the exclusion side, so a subject who returns 80 for thr-count-080 answers both."],"objections":["thr-meaning-choice is a duplicate of thr-count-080: both turn on the single rule 'threshold is the fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS'. Once thr-count-080 stopped supplying that definition in its stem, the recognition case ceased to add independent evidence; it was counted in the earlier review only because the then-existing open cases leaked or presupposed that definition.","thr-outliers-choice is likewise a duplicate of thr-count-080 (and of thr-meaning-choice): 'some molecules were now left out due to the set threshold' is the same fact as 'only 80 of 100 are guaranteed to contain it', asked from the exclusion side, which the rubric names explicitly as a duplicate pattern.","oracle_independence relies on an 'RDKit C++ FMCS.h source listing' with Threshold initialised to 1.0 and the inline comment 'match all molecules' to anchor thr-count-default's semantics, but evidence.references contains only the rdFMCS Python API page and the TeachOpenCADD talktorial. The byte-level verification therefore does not cover the step that makes 145 the correct answer; the quoted bytes establish only that the set has 145 molecules.","thr-relaxed-size prints both reported sizes (24 and 28 atoms) in its stem, so it is effectively a two-way discrimination presented in generated form. With 3 trials, blind guessing passes about one time in eight, so the case is materially weaker than its open answer form suggests.","The justification's stronger_grade_considered treats the removal of the two previously criticised cases as sufficient to reach A, without re-auditing the two retained cases against the revised set; the earlier 'counts' verdicts on them were given for a design in which the open cases leaked, so they cannot be carried forward unexamined."],"required_revisions":["Replace thr-meaning-choice and thr-outliers-choice with cases that turn on in-scope facts not already tested by thr-count-080, or accept a three-counting-case design at grade B.","Add to evidence.references the RDKit source or documentation page that actually shows the default Threshold value of 1.0 and its 'match all molecules' semantics, so that thr-count-default's expected answer rests on pinned, quote-verified bytes rather than on an uncited listing.","Rewrite thr-relaxed-size so the correct value is not one of two numbers printed in the stem (for example, report only one run's size and ask for a property of the other run that follows from the relaxation), so that it is not answerable by a coin flip."],"case_verdicts":[{"case_id":"thr-count-080","verdict":"counts","reason":"The stem gives only the call and the set size and never says what threshold means, so the subject must supply the fraction-of-the-dataset semantics and apply it; the expected count is the exact quantitative content of the claim's first assertion.","replacement":""},{"case_id":"thr-count-default","verdict":"counts","reason":"Requires two facts the stem does not supply - that the default threshold is 1.0 and that 1.0 requires every input molecule to contain the MCS - so it is not answerable from thr-count-080 alone and tests the other side of the claim's contrast.","replacement":""},{"case_id":"thr-relaxed-size","verdict":"counts","reason":"Tests the direction of the claim's outlier-tolerance assertion (relaxing the requirement can admit a larger common core) rather than the fraction rule itself, and the stem does not say which reported result came from which run. It counts, though its evidential weight is reduced because both candidate values appear in the stem.","replacement":""},{"case_id":"thr-meaning-choice","verdict":"duplicate","reason":"Turns on the same rule as the earlier thr-count-080 - threshold is the fraction of the dataset that must contain the MCS - merely asked in recognition form; a subject who answers 80 for a 100-molecule set at threshold=0.8 will select that option here, so it adds no independent evidence.","replacement":"A generated case that applies the fraction rule where it is not simply a round multiplication: give a bare FindMCS(mols, threshold=0.8) call over a set whose size makes 80% non-integral (for example a series of 7 or 23 analogues) and ask for the minimum number of those molecules the returned MCS is guaranteed to be contained in, with no sentence in the stem describing what threshold means. This stays inside the claim because it probes the same 80%-of-the-input-structures requirement, but it cannot be answered by the rounded arithmetic of thr-count-080 and it forces the subject to commit to how the fraction is applied at the boundary. It must be anchored in RDKit source or documentation that states the rounding behaviour, not inferred.","case_id_note":""},{"case_id":"thr-outliers-choice","verdict":"duplicate","reason":"Turns on the same rule as the earlier thr-count-080, asked from the exclusion side: 'some molecules were now left out due to the set threshold' is the complement of 'only 80 of 100 are guaranteed to contain the MCS', which the rubric names as a duplicate pattern rather than an independent test.","replacement":"A generated case that distinguishes a set-level guarantee from a per-molecule one: state that a 145-analogue set was run at threshold=0.8 and that the returned MCS was recorded, then name one particular molecule of the set and ask whether that specific molecule is guaranteed to contain the returned substructure, and how the answer differs for the default run. This stays inside the claim because it tests the same 0.8-versus-1.0 requirement the claim asserts, but it turns on the existential-versus-universal character of the guarantee rather than on restating the 80% count, so a subject who merely recalls 'threshold is a fraction' need not get it right."}]}
